payload.title: Full-repository scan as an explicit option, not part of the git hooks
payload.description:
LeftBlock checks only staged changes in its git hooks. That catches new leaks, but not ones already sitting in a repo. Found 2026-10-23: an author email in Markus's pyproject.toml had been in the repo all along; LeftBlock passed the commit that removed it, because it never saw the line in a diff.

## Want
An explicit, opt-in way to scan whole files: the entire working tree, or chosen paths. It must NOT be built into the git hooks. The hooks stay diff-only and fast. A full scan runs only when asked, for example `leftblock scan --all` or `leftblock scan PATH…`, and suits a one-off audit or a CI job a repo opts into.

## Scope (to decide when picked up)
- The CLI shape: a flag, or a subcommand.
- The same rule set and allow-list (.leftblock-allow.yml) as the hooks, including the role-address allowance.
- Respect .gitignore and ignore_paths; skip binaries and lockfiles by default.
- Output: findings with file:line, a non-zero exit when anything is found, and a machine-readable JSON format.
- Optional: a baseline file, so existing accepted findings don't block, if needed.

## Acceptance
- Gherkin specs (narrative, complete): a full scan finds a pre-existing email that a diff scan misses; the hooks still scan diffs only; allow-listed entries are skipped; the exit codes.
- README documents when to use each.

Filed only. Not started; no work scheduled.
